themes_ranked.plan_rule: Treat the new booking push as the top priority: send it as high priority and check delivery on Android.
Move upgrade asks out of push into an in-app message at the moment the limit is hit.
Hold marketing pushes to the computed cap and let owners choose which booking alerts they get.
No marketing push in quiet hours; send scheduled pushes in the user's own time zone.
Add notification categories (Android channels and an in-app settings screen) so one type can be turned off alone.

reviews.method: Reviews that mention notification, push, alert, ping, buzz or reminder, sorted into five themes by their words; one review can hit more than one theme.

timing.quiet_rule: each holds under 1.5% of the day's active users
timing.time_zone_note: GA4 hours are in the property time zone (America/New_York). Send scheduled pushes by each user's local time in the push provider.

permission_prompt.why: The earliest step that a planned push directly serves (new booking and cancellation alerts start from here) and that at least 50% of new users reach.
permission_prompt.now: first launch, before sign-up (iOS and Android); dashboard page load (web)

soft_ask.title: Know the moment a client books
soft_ask.body: Get an alert the moment a client books or cancels. Pick which alerts you want on the alerts screen.

flow: Show the soft ask once the booking page is published; only a tap on Turn on alerts opens the system prompt. It is the only message at that moment: the calendar in-app waits for the first dashboard open at least 12 hours later.
On Not now: no system prompt. Offer the soft ask again after the first booking arrives, then no more than once every 30 days, at most twice.
iOS: the system prompt shows once; after a denial, the only way back is a Settings link on the alerts screen.
Android: the app targets Android 15, so it controls the timing; check that notifications are enabled before each send.
Web: ask only after a click on a bell icon on the bookings screen, never on page load.

option_ios_provisional.why: Provisional authorization delivers every push quietly to Notification Center (no banner, no sound) until the owner allows full alerts. The first alert here is the new booking push, a time-sensitive alert the owner wants to see at once, and the top review complaint is 'missing or late', so a quiet first booking alert would make it worse. The soft ask after publishing asks for full alerts instead.

caps.method: Load = marketing pushes delivered ÷ opted-in devices. Churn = opt-outs + Android uninstalls (GA4 app_remove) per 1,000 opted-in devices. A load passes while churn stays at or under 2x the quietest bucket (a starting point); daily buckets need 5 days, weekly buckets 2 weeks.
caps.not_counted: Pushes the user chose in the alerts screen (new booking, cancellation, today's schedule) don't count toward the marketing cap.
caps.gap: iOS uninstalls are not in the export (the provider has no uninstall tracking), so iOS churn is opt-outs only.

rules: Time-sensitive and the user is away from the app: push.
Needs the user on a screen to act: in-app, shown on that screen.
Long, kept for later or a record: email.
One primary channel per moment; a second channel only as a fallback after a wait, when the first was not acted on.
One moment, one message: the permission soft ask is alone at its trigger; another message on that trigger waits for a later session.
An email flow on the same trigger within 24 hours stacks with the push or in-app; move one.

findings: Only 44.5% of iOS devices and 58.3% of Android 13+ devices can get a push, because the prompt shows at first launch before sign-up. Move it to after booking_page_published (51.6% of new users get there) behind a soft ask.
Marketing pushes cost devices: churn is 2.59x the quiet-day level on days with 1 to 2 pushes per device. Cap marketing at 1 a day and 4 a week; 9 of the last 84 days went over the daily cap.
Store reviews: the top notification complaint is missing or late (7 reviews). Treat the new booking push as the top priority: send it as high priority and check delivery on Android.
Push P4 (Finish your booking page) fires 24 hours after sign-up, the same moment as the Klaviyo email, and reaches almost no one (260 delivered in 28 days). Stop it; the email carries that moment.
The upgrade push (P6) opens at 1.4% and draws promotional complaints; replace it with an in-app message when the staff limit is reached.

The calendar in-app (I1) shows on every dashboard open and gets 3.0% clicks with 72.4% dismissed; show it once, on the first dashboard open at least 12 hours after the page goes live (the soft ask has the publish moment), and again after a double booking, not on every open.
unknowns: Opt-outs per message (the export gives daily totals, so churn is matched to days, not to single pushes).
Users' local time zones (GA4 hours are in the property time zone).
